name: Shechi: A Secure Distributed Computation Compiler Based on Multiparty Homomorphic Encryption
summary: A compiler for multiparty homomorphic encryption pipelines, written by the Sequre authors and built as a Codon extension: the artifact carries Codon IR helpers in C++ alongside 88 .codon files, 87 of whose paths it shares with Sequre. Codon is the substrate the whole system compiles through, and Shechi is the most recent work in the Codon lineage that extends the compiler rather than calling it.
why_codon: The work is a compiler built on Codon's IR, by the group that also wrote Sequre and co-authored the Codon paper.
note: The only work in the corpus citing four anchors. Has no paper DOI; six Zenodo artifact DOIs exist instead.

name: An Empirical Study on the Performance and Energy Usage of Compiled Python Code
summary: A measurement study of what compiling Python actually buys, running seven benchmarks through eight tools -- PyPy, Numba, Nuitka, Mypyc, Codon, Cython, Pyston-lite and the experimental 3.13 build -- against CPython on two machines, recording energy, execution time and memory while varying CPU frequency and core count. Codon is one of the eight subjects, so the paper measures it rather than using or extending it, and it is the only work in the corpus that reports Codon's energy consumption as well as its speed.
why_codon: The paper states its subject is comparing the performance and energy efficiency of Python compilers, and names Codon among the eight it compiles with.
note: The natural companion to the repository-side benchmark entries. Where mce-sandbox and word-counter time Codon informally, this does it as a controlled study.

name: Pyls: Enabling Python Hardware Synthesis with Dynamic Polymorphism via LCRS Encoding
summary: A high-level synthesis framework that compiles dynamically polymorphic Python into monolithic hardware by representing every object as a Left-Child Right-Sibling tree, generating XLS IR and resolving types at runtime through a tree memory architecture, reporting large speedups over CPU and soft-core baselines on FPGA. Its own pipeline is XLS rather than Codon; Codon appears as prior work in the same problem area, one of the existing solutions the paper positions against for supporting only a static subset of Python.
why_codon: Abstract only; the paper's own toolchain is XLS IR and nothing indicates Codon runs. Inferred from the framing against existing solutions that support static subsets of Python that Codon is cited as prior art rather than used.
needs: Confirm against the full text that Codon is not run. Read from the abstract only.

name: PopPy: Opportunistically Exploiting Parallelism in Python Compound AI Applications
summary: A system that finds parallelism in Python applications whose runtime is dominated by calls out to machine-learning models, on the argument that traditional optimizing compilers cannot help when execution time sits in external components. Codon is cited from that framing, as one of the language optimization systems whose assumptions the paper departs from, rather than as part of PopPy's own implementation.
why_codon: Abstract only. Inferred from the paper's central claim -- that optimizing compilers cannot address latency dominated by external calls -- that Codon is cited as an instance of the approach being departed from.
needs: Confirm the citation context against the full text. Read from the abstract only.

name: UniTe: A Universal Tensor Abstraction for Capturing Spatial Relationships
summary: An abstraction for spatial relationships between tensors defined against a common coordinate system, where the tensors differ in axes, spacing, origin and shape, addressing the bookkeeping users currently do by hand because no language support exists for these semantics. The abstract does not say what the abstraction is implemented in, so whether Codon is the host language or is cited as related language-design work is not yet established.
why_codon: Not established. The abstract describes a lack of language support for tensor semantics but does not name an implementation language.
